A refinement involving three mutual information terms gives the exact minimum of the weighted sum at fixed entropies of the two parties and of their union, attained by at most three independent bipartite pure states. This criterion recovers the cycle and complete-graph inequalities and shows that uniform incidence parity, which we prove sufficient for polygon inequalities on hypergraphs, is not necessary. Averaging strong subadditivity over both sides of a bipartition gives a sharp $k$-marginal inequality with coefficient $2\binom{n-2}{k-1}$, and we determine uniformly optimal coefficients for collective hyperstar inequalities. For paths and overlapping hyperchains, the deficits are exact sums of conditional mutual information terms; genuinely multipartite entangled cluster states saturate the hyperchain inequality while the chain inequality remains strict. We characterize pure chain equality states, bound the trace distance to cycle equality states independently of the number of parties and local dimensions, and obtain bond-dimension bounds for matrix product states and sequential-recovery error estimates.

title: A plane-wave auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo study of silicon point defects
summary: Accurately predicting the energetics of point defects remains a formidable challenge in computational materials science. For the tetrahedral silicon self-interstitial, for example, previous periodic coupled-cluster [CCSD(T)] and diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) calculations disagree by about 1.2 eV. Here, we present formation energies of silicon self-interstitials and vacancies using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) in a plane-wave basis formulated within the projector-augmented wave framework, and compare them with the random-phase approximation (RPA) and CCSD(T). Using 16- and 64-atom cells, we demonstrate that an RPA-based correction effectively removes the two-body finite-size errors that remain after twist averaging in AFQMC for bulk silicon and for the dumbbell and hexagonal self-interstitials. With this correction, we obtain formation energies of 4.4 eV and 4.6 eV for these two self-interstitials in 16-atom cells, in good agreement with DMC and transcorrelated coupled-cluster results. For the tetrahedral interstitial and the Jahn--Teller-distorted vacancy, 16-atom cells are too small to obtain realistic formation energies; in 64-atom cells, we obtain 5.7 eV and 5.2 eV, respectively. With identical setups in 16-atom cells, CCSD(T) yields systematically lower formation energies than AFQMC, with the largest difference, 250 meV, for the tetrahedral interstitial. Our results indicate that the earlier overestimation of CCSD(T) for the tetrahedral interstitial stems from the finite-size treatment in the coupled-cluster workflow rather than from multi-configurational character of the defect.

title: Compact GridPix Tracking: Test Beam Performance and Detector Response Modelling
summary: We characterise a Timepix-based GridPix detector with a 21 mm drift length using 2.6 GeV electrons at ELSA. Tracks entering through the window at several angles are reconstructed as compact $μ$TPC tracklets, providing position and local direction from one layer. Measured angular widths are approximately 5--10 mrad. An empirical response model calibrated to these data augments Geant4 ionisation information with gas-transport and readout effects, reproducing ten of twelve angular widths within approximately 20% and all spatial-residual widths within approximately 12%. Application without re-tuning to an independent 5 mm-drift measurement shows larger angular discrepancies. Our response model therefore provides input to feasibility studies of future compact tracking detectors.

title: Gyromagnetic ratios of slowly rotating charged Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes
summary: Charged Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes, supported by a phantom scalar field in Einstein--Maxwell theory, connect two asymptotically flat regions, so a rotating member carries a magnetic dipole moment and a gyromagnetic ratio at each mouth. We construct the slowly rotating family in closed form on all three background branches and show that, within the stationary axial dipole sector and with no applied magnetic field, the first-order solution is unique. The two gyromagnetic ratios obey an exact deficit relation set by the static geometry alone. It gives $g_\pm<2$ at both mouths, bounds the deficit by two-thirds of the squared ratio of scalar to electric charge, and, through the positivity of the reduced magnetic moment, gives each ratio the sign of the mass of its own mouth; the two ratios coincide only for reflection-symmetric throats, so their difference measures the asymmetry of the wormhole. Rotation drags the two ends relative to each other in a definite sense, with a dragging profile that decreases monotonically across the throat, and the electromagnetic field carries a strictly positive share of the angular momentum on every finite sphere. Toward the extremal edge at the positive mouth the deficit closes cubically on every trajectory studied, because the redshift factor at the throat vanishes quadratically; the coefficient depends on the path. When the charge is switched off, the frame dragging reproduces known neutral results, whereas on the massive neutral branch the gyromagnetic ratios stay away from the Kerr--Newman value.

title: Calabi-Yau linear models with abelian bundles
summary: We introduce a construction of (0,2) gauged linear sigma models whose large radius phases realize Calabi-Yau sigma models with line bundles. We study a family of such models admitting Landau-Ginzburg orbifold phases, described as asymmetric orbifolds of (2,2) Gepner models and free left-moving fermions. These orbifolds extend the Gepner construction to a broader class of (0,2) SCFTs, and reveal unexpected features, including the emergence of free fermions in twisted sectors and substantial enhancements of the left-moving current algebra. The gauged linear sigma model connects the Calabi-Yau geometry to these rational points, where the volume modulus becomes charged under the enhanced gauge symmetry and freezes at the string scale.

title: Topological (in)equivalence encoded in zeros of wavefunction overlaps
summary: Topological equivalence between two gapped band structures is determined by whether their occupied states can be continuously deformed into one another without closing the energy gap or breaking the protecting symmetries. We show that this relative topology can be read directly from the overlap matrix between the two occupied subspaces, in a way that treats Chern and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants within a single framework. The determinant of the overlap matrix defines a global section of a line bundle over the Brillouin zone, which vanishes at the momenta where the map between the subspaces fails to be invertible. A singular connection, whose curvature is concentrated at these zeros, assigns each zero an integer charge given by its phase winding. In two-dimensional class A, the total charge equals the difference between the Chern numbers of the two systems. In class AII, time reversal pairs zeros of opposite charge, and the relative $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant is the parity of the total charge in half the Brillouin zone; the Kane-Mele Pfaffian is recovered as a special case. The zeros coincide with the gap closings of an interpolation between the two systems, and crystalline symmetries constrain their positions and charges. We illustrate the construction in the Haldane, Kane-Mele, and Qi-Wu-Zhang models, including cases where rotation symmetry alone enforces the zeros.

title: Machine Learning-Driven High-Throughput Screening of Equimolar and Non-Equimolar High-Entropy Carbides
summary: Search for optimal compositions among high-entropy ceramics are challenging due to large composition space, which are unable to test either experimentally or by \textit{ab initio} calculations. Here we present a high-throughput screening for equimolar and non-equimolar high-entropy carbides (HEC) among group IVB and VB transition metals (Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb and Ta). Large Atomistic Model MACE, and deep learning based interatomic potential DeePMD trained on \textit{ab initio}-based dataset of structures are used to effectively screen over the thousands of potential non-equimolar compositions among high-entropy carbides of Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb and Ta transition metals. A set of both equimolar and non-equimolar HECs are predicted to be stable in order to further synthesize those compositions based on the predictions.

title: Future avenues for precision oscillation measurements with compact movable reactors
comment: 13 pages main body, 20 pages total, 11 figures Comments are welcome!
summary: No planned neutrino experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on $\thone$. Doing so requires innovative strategies to reduce statistical and systematic uncertainties. In this study, we consider a futuristic program with a movable reactor antineutrino source placed within short distances ($L\lesssim 3\,\km$) from the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) detector. Due to the large fiducial mass of JUNO, even a relatively small reactor can produce a statistically significant number of events over a few years to probe the $\lesssim 8.7\% \,\nuebar$ disappearance set by $\thone$. We consider two possibilities: a $\mathcal{O}(20\mwth)$ microreactor in alcoves of the access tunnel to the underground laboratory, and a $\mathcal{O}(400 \mwth)$ unit on the surface. In both cases the reactor is observed by a small flux monitor detector near the source, while JUNO measures the antineutrino flux at two baselines, suppressing correlated flux and detector systematics. Using the measured Daya Bay per-isotope spectra and its covariance, we model a high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) core for the microreactor and a low-enriched uranium (LEU) core for the surface unit, and discuss various potential sources of systematic uncertainties and their impact on the precision of $\thone$. The underground microreactor could improve on JUNO's reach by a factor of three to four, to $\relsth \simeq 4\%$ over a decade, while the surface reactor would reach the present global-fit precision, $\relsth=2.5\%$, in about three years, provided the emission rate is monitored across reactor relocations to the sub-percent level.

title: Numerical Implementation and Tests of the Quadratic Effective Action for Lorentzian Spinfoam Amplitudes
summary: In the pure integral representation of Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitudes, the integration over non-geometric variables in the large-spin limit defines an effective action for Regge geometries. Expanding this effective action to quadratic order around a flat background recovers the classical Regge action $iS_{\mathrm{Regge}}$ at leading order, supplemented by a curvature correction quadratic in the bulk deficit angles $\varepsilon$. In this work, we numerically implement this effective-action framework and validate its analytic predictions using two Julia packages: LorentzianSimplexSolver, for the computation of real and complex critical-point data, and Effective-Spinfoam, for the evaluation of the effective action. We apply this workflow to the double-$Δ_3$ complex, the $1$-$5$ Pachner move, its refinement, and a $24$-simplex hypercube triangulation. Two complementary numerical tests are performed: first, starting from the real critical point of a flat background, we verify that the leading term reproduces the quadratic Regge action and evaluate the $\varepsilon^2$ curvature correction across a range of the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $γ$. Power-law fits confirm that in the small-$γ$ regime, the $\varepsilon^2$ correction is of higher order in $γ$ than the Regge action. Second, for a sample of curved geometries with finite length perturbations $δ\ell$, we numerically solve the full nonlinear critical equations at fixed perturbed edge lengths for complex critical points. By comparing the direct action evaluation at complex critical points with the quadratic effective action, we demonstrate that the latter accurately reproduces the nonlinear complex critical-point action up to remainders of cubic order in $δ\ell$.

title: From Instantons to AdS Boundaries: Tracing the Geometric Path from Quantum Anomalies to Massive Gravity
summary: This thesis studies how boundary data enter two gravitational observables: the Dirac index on gravitational instantons and conserved charges in three-dimensional New Massive Gravity. In Einstein gravity coupled to ModMax electrodynamics, we compute the index of charged Dirac fermions on Taub-NUT and Eguchi-Hanson instantons using the Atiyah-Patodi-Singer theorem, which includes the spectral asymmetry of the boundary Dirac operator. The Taub-NUT index agrees with the Maxwell result. For Eguchi-Hanson, the gauge-field contribution to the axial anomaly depends explicitly on the ModMax parameter when expressed in terms of the solution parameters. For asymptotically anti-de Sitter solutions of New Massive Gravity with Brown-Henneaux boundary conditions, a term linear in the extrinsic curvature reproduces the holographic stress tensor of the auxiliary-field formulation. At the degenerate point, relaxed boundary conditions admit an additional constrained Fefferman-Graham coefficient. A quadratic extrinsic counterterm cancels the residual power divergence. We derive the boundary Ward identity and show that the holographic and Noether-Wald charges agree for the solutions studied.

title: Certified Discovery of Quantum Phase Diagrams
summary: Can a machine provably discover new quantum phases of matter? We show that the answer is yes under physically motivated assumptions. For any smooth family of geometrically local Hamiltonians, we construct an efficient quantum algorithm that outputs the phase diagram to prescribed accuracy and provides a verifiable certificate for every transition it reports. The algorithm takes as input only a classical description of the family together with unverified preparations of reference ground states; no order parameter, symmetry-breaking pattern, or training data are supplied. It succeeds provided that at least one preparation is correct in each gapped region of parameter space. The algorithm explores parameter space by quasi-adiabatically or adiabatically transporting each reference state, detecting the approach of a phase boundary by tapping the transported state with a frequency-filtered local probe: excitations created by the probe witness the closing of the energy gap. We prove that the gap closing for continuous phase transitions can always be detected using the frequency-filtered gradient of the Hamiltonian. The gap-detecting measurement is gentle, so when the ground state is unique a single reusable copy of each reference ground state supports the full exploration (for degenerate ground states, polynomially many copies suffice). The quantum algorithm runs in polynomial time at inverse-polynomial gap resolution. We also give a classical algorithm that runs in quasipolynomial time at constant gap resolution. Numerical experiments demonstrate how our algorithm accurately determines the phase structure of several model quantum systems.

title: The phase diagram of fluid hydrogen near melting from machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on quantum Monte Carlo
summary: Dissociation of molecular hydrogen increasing temperature or pressure may either occur gradually or abruptly, via a phase transition. Despite considerable experimental and theoretical efforts, the phase diagram of dense hydrogen at temperatures above solid melting is not precisely known. Here, we perform classical and quantum Path Integral molecular dynamics simulations of dense hydrogen using two machine-learned interatomic potentials both trained on quantum Monte Carlo energies and forces. The resulting phase diagram is constructed using state-of-the-art techniques. Both models show a first-order phase transition from the molecular to the atomic liquid terminating in critical points whose locations were determined using finite-size scaling techniques. Triple points, located at the highest temperature of the melting curve, are found at the intersection of the liquid-liquid lines with the melting curve and should lead to clear signatures in ramp compression experiments.

title: Pure integral formula of spinfoam amplitude and curvature corrections in effective theory
summary: We develop a new analytic method for the semiclassical analysis of the Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitude on a fixed triangulation. We derive a pure integral formula for the spinfoam amplitude that trades the discrete sum over internal spins for integrals over continuous variables. This reformulation is free of discrete sums and provides a well-behaved action that is well-adapted to the stationary phase approximation in the large-spin regime. Integrating out the non-geometric variables yields an effective action for the edge lengths of the Regge geometry. Applying the stationary phase approximation and expanding this effective action to second order in perturbations around a flat background, we obtain the classical Regge action at leading order, supplemented by a quadratic correction in the deficit angles $\varepsilon$. This curvature correction originates from two distinct sources: a holonomy correction resulting from the new action and the fluctuations of non-Regge areas. We show that the quadratic $\varepsilon$ correction appears at a higher order in the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $γ$ relative to the Regge action. Together with the large-spin expansion, this yields a two-parameter expansion for the spinfoam effective action, whose leading order is the quadratic Regge action. In the long wavelength regime, the latter approaches the action of a massless spin-2 graviton.

title: Holographic Duals of $SL^{(q)}(2, \mathbb{R})$ Deformed CFTs
summary: We study the holographic bulk dual of 2D CFTs evolved by $sl^{(q)}(2,R)$-deformed Hamiltonians. Working in the Hamiltonian-adapted frame, in which the $sl^{(q)}(2,R)$-deformed effective Floquet Hamiltonian generates time translations, we construct the dual Bañados geometries for the three distinct classes of dynamics: the heating phase, the non-heating phase and the phase boundary. Specifically, we show that in the heating phase, the bulk patch dual to the region between two neighbouring fixed points has a time-dependent causal horizon and asymptotes to a static AdS Rindler geometry at late times, while the non-heating phase has no horizon. We discuss how the late-time behaviour of the entanglement entropy, particularly its linear growth in the heating phase, can be understood from the bulk in two different ways: in global AdS, from the portion of the geodesic behind the horizons, and in a quotient description, from an effective shockwave produced by a boosted conical defect. Finally, for ($q=1$), we complete the holographic analysis of Ref. [1] by reproducing the exact CFT expression of the OTOC from the bulk and explaining why it exhibits an exponential growth {\it only} when the operators lie on the side of the two fixed points.

title: The Markov Property on Decorated Metric Planar Maps
comment: This paper together with https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05447 were originally only one paper that was uploaded to ArXiv on May 2025, so before the AI craziness of 2026. Thanks to the comments of some referees we decided to separate the original paper into two parts
summary: We introduce decorated metric planar maps: planar maps whose edges $e$ are replaced by segments $[0,w_e]$, together with a continuous function on the resulting metric space, the decoration. We consider laws under which, conditionally on the metric map, the decoration follows a statistical physics model such as the Ising model or the Gaussian free field: the values at the vertices interact through a quadratic Hamiltonian and, given these values, the decoration along each edge is a Brownian bridge. Working with 4-regular maps with a boundary (the duals of quadrangulations with a boundary), we define a Markov property that allows explorations to stop in the middle of an edge. We show that, under mild regularity assumptions, the rerooting-invariant families of laws satisfying this Markov property are exactly the Boltzmann decorated metric maps. We also prove a strong Markov property and show that the random submaps inducing a Markovian decomposition are exactly the stopping maps for a suitable filtration. Finally, we obtain analogous results for classical decorated planar maps.

title: A Symmetry-Stratified Framework for Phase Transitions: Thermodynamic States, Critical Dynamics, and Spectral Mechanical Signatures
summary: Structural symmetry, thermodynamic phase stability, and elastic-wave response provide related but distinct descriptions of a transforming solid. We formulate a symmetry-stratified framework that connects these descriptions through a finite-dimensional internal state and a parent-invariant free energy. Stabilizers classify structural states, whereas free-energy comparisons and stability conditions determine equilibrium branches and dissipative evolution. Equivariance ensures that the frozen elastic tangent inherits the structural stabilizer. Equality requires additional identifiability conditions. Little-group representations and degenerate perturbation theory then determine whether an acoustic doublet splits and the first nonzero splitting order $p$. On a selected continuous branch with order-parameter exponent $β$, a regular, observable acoustic gap scales as $|t|^{pβ}$, provided critical self-energies and structural relaxation do not dominate the measurement. Explicit tensorial and cubic-to-tetragonal realizations yield linear and quadratic splitting channels, together with directionally protected degeneracies. Separate numerical benchmarks examine free-energy reconstruction, coexistence, elastic compatibility, finite-temperature spectra, and controlled critical readouts. Reanalysis of NiTi measurements illustrates effective elastic degeneracy, thermal-history dependence, and the predictive value of independently measured phase fractions. Most importantly, the framework identifies the constitutive and measurement assumptions required to infer structural changes from mechanical spectra.

title: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
summary: Detecting subsolar objects in binary mergers would be an exceptional discovery in gravitational wave astronomy. So far, dedicated searches for subsolar coalescences reported no confident detections, setting upper bounds on their merger rate. Given that standard stellar evolution is not able to produce subsolar candidates, a confident detection would point either to new physics or to unconventional astrophysical pathways. These include collapsars, where the outer parts of neutrino-cooled accretion disks around newborn stellar-mass black holes are subject to fragmentation and give rise to subsolar neutron stars, which can later merge with the central black hole. We show that current subsolar searches may miss a significant fraction of these neutron star-black hole mergers, because their templates do not account for the small mass ratios, the tidal disruption of the neutron star, and the effects of the surrounding gas. This result motivates improving the waveform modeling used in current subsolar searches and building adequate template banks tailored to these systems.

title: Upper Bounds on the Radion Mass in a Warped Extra Dimension
summary: We study absolute upper bounds on the mass ratio $R_{11}=m_{r_1}/m_{h_1}$ between the radion ($r_1$) and graviton ($h_1$) lightest modes in five dimensional warped models. We consider warped models with an admissible singular behavior in the infrared: i.e.~models with power-like ($\sim \barφ^{2n}$) and with exponential ($\sim e^{2ν\barφ}$) bulk potentials, where $\barφ$ is the stabilizing bulk field. We find a correlation between $R_{11}$ and the singular behavior of the Ricci scalar, which allows to establish an absolute upper bound on the former. For the power-like models, the maximum value of $R_{11}$ increases with $n$. In the limit $n\to\infty$, the power-like model reproduces the exponential model and reaches the same upper bound as the latter. For the exponential model, we derive analytically the bound $R_{11}<1$, with the largest value approached for the case $ν\to 1^+$ (where $ν=1$ corresponds to the linear dilaton model) and consistent with unitarity sum rules. For exponential models we also obtain the absolute upper bound on the second radion mode ratio $R_{21}=m_{r_2}/m_{h_1}\lesssim 1.374$. This value is reached for $ν=2$ when the IR brane approaches the singularity. For this configuration, we verify that the scalar contribution satisfies the unitarity sum rule when the complete radion Kaluza-Klein tower is included.

title: A Computational and Experimental Framework for Fourier Optics in Python
summary: Simulation of the propagation of light is useful for the design and dimensioning of optical systems. In this paper, we present the basics of propagation simulation using Fourier optics and practical implementation in Python, with a particular emphasis on dimensions. We first verify that our numerical wave-optics simulations maintain correct physical spatial scaling. Next, we benchmark numerical propagation against closed-form analytical formulas for Gaussian beams, lens focusing effects, and grating diffraction. We then show how those simulations can be used to generate diffractive optical elements such as Fresnel zone plates, and we bridge the gap between numerical simulations and experiments by collecting data and recovering phase information using a phase retrieval algorithm.

title: Single-Crystal Growth, Structure, and Physical Properties of Yb2MoO6
summary: Rare-earth molybdates are functional oxides of considerable interest because their structural and chemical flexibility enables diverse magnetic, electronic, and optical behavior. Here, millimeter-sized single crystals of $Yb_2MoO_6$ are synthesized, their crystal structure determined and physical properties investigated. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms the formation of $Yb_2MoO_6$ and yielded lattice parameters of $a = 16.228(2)$ $\mathring{A}$, $b = 10.901(3)$ $\mathring{A}$, and $c = 5.286(2)$ $\mathring{A}$, in good agreement with previously reported neutron powder diffraction data. Scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive spectroscopy show a Yb:Mo ratio close to the expected 2:1 stoichiometry. Optical measurements based on diffuse-reflectance spectra and Tauc analysis yield an estimated optical gap of $\sim 3.28$ eV under the direct-allowed transition assumption. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal Curie-Weiss-like paramagnetic behavior, with an effective magnetic moment of $μ_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 4.2μ_B$ per Yb and an apparent Weiss temperature of $θ\approx -65.7$ K, consistent with possible antiferromagnetic interactions or correlations, with no clear magnetic-ordering transition observed down to 10 K. These results establish the growth of $Yb_2MoO_6$ single crystals and provide initial insight into their structural, optical, and magnetic properties.

title: Strong Coupling of Cosmological Perturbations in mLQC-I: The Hybrid Approach
summary:
We study nonlinear perturbative consistency of scalar perturbations in modified loop quantum cosmology I (mLQC-I) within the hybrid approach. We express the quadratic and cubic Hamiltonians in a common canonical representation before imposing the background constraint and adopt a minimal sector-preserving cubic regularization. Near the pre-bounce quantum-geometrical de Sitter phase, nonlinear coefficients become strongly enhanced. The $α_I^3/κ$ term survives the leading ultraviolet cubic kernel for fixed nondegenerate triangles in the selected frequency assignment. This enhancement occurs in four inflationary potentials, with formal suppression scales sensitive to their normalization. In an assumed factorized quartic continuation, a selected lapse contact does not cancel enhanced cubic exchange in an analytic scattering family. However, the derived quartic Legendre contribution cancels that lapse contact at $V=K_φ$ in the Hamiltonian. The full amplitude remains unresolved: omitted quartic sectors are not proved subleading, and the formal scales do not determine a physical cutoff.
  For an instantaneous quadratic state initialized at the bounce, the equilateral cubic diagnostic first reaches unity at $K\simeq0.6483m_{\rm P}$. Evolution over $0\le t/t_{\rm P}\le10$ lowers this crossing to $K\simeq0.64626m_{\rm P}$. Sampled shape and independent frequency-assignment tests do not lower these thresholds. A fourth-order adiabatic ultraviolet tail can be attached without changing the tested finite modes. These results identify pre-bounce nonlinear enhancement and a candidate bounce-state window. Broader evolution and shape tests, renormalized backreaction, observational mode mapping on a consistently normalized background, and a complete fourth-order theory remain necessary to establish interacting consistency.

title: Pairwise fermionic mode correlations in electric and magnetic backgrounds: Landau-level structure and Schwinger production
summary: We investigate mutual information and logarithmic negativity in fermionic Schwinger pair production in parallel electric and magnetic fields. Using spin-dependent Bogoliubov transformations, we construct the in-vacuum and derive the particle--antiparticle correlations for selected Landau modes. We also consider an initially entangled two-particle state and evaluate the correlations for six bipartitions. The physical Landau-level structure is treated explicitly by distinguishing modes with the same oscillator index from the spin representatives of a common physical Landau level. For matched higher levels, the pairwise redistribution relations retain the electric-only form, with the magnetic-field dependence entering through the Landau-level pair-production probabilities. When the two particle groups occupy different physical levels, the cross particle--antiparticle correlations become unequal, and we derive analytic relations characterizing this asymmetry. We further obtain the local logarithmic negativity from the ordinary partial transpose in a fixed occupation-space basis. Finally, we extend the analysis to a Sauter-type electric field in a constant magnetic background and examine the dependence of the pairwise correlations on the field parameters and Landau-level structure.

title: Nodal Knotted Finite-Energy Spatiotemporally Localized Scalar Wave Solutions
summary: Significant amount of information is available in wave optics about monochromatic paraxial beams characterized by nodal knots, the latter being threads of complete darkness (lines of zero intensity) tied into knots. Also, well -known are finite-energy spatiotemporally localized vector-valued wave solutions characterized by knotted to-pologies. Unfortunately, except for solutions to the Schrödinger-like equation describing anomalous dispersion, no scalar-valued spatiotemporally localized waves with analogous knotted topological structures are known to date. It is the goal in this article to fill in this gap by deriving finite-energy spatiotemporally localized scalar-valued wave solutions characterized specifically by Hopf and trefoil nodal knot topologies. This will extend to spatiotemporally localized pulsed fields the diverse important applications of mono-chromatic light beams, having nontrivial topological structures, in trapping and guiding particles, image processing and optical communications; also, in applications to biology and medicine.

title: Molecular engineering for crack-free transfer of single-crystalline oxide membranes onto silicon
summary: Heterogeneous integration of single-crystalline complex oxides with silicon offers a route to incorporating their functionalities into next-generation microelectronics. Released from their growth substrates, freestanding oxide membranes enable this integration. However, cracks, wrinkles, and fragmentation during release and transfer limit membrane size and quality. Here, we present an interfacial energy-controlled release strategy that enables crack-free, single-crystalline freestanding oxide membranes with centimeter-scale lateral dimensions. Using SrTiO3 as a model system, time-resolved release studies identify water-induced blistering at the membrane-support interface during prolonged water exposure as the origin of membrane cracking. Lowering the molecular weight of the poly(propylene carbonate) support through polymer deconstruction increases its polarity and surface energy, suppresses interfacial blistering, and reduces organic residue after support removal. The resulting SrTiO3 membranes exhibit optical properties comparable to those of bulk single crystals. We extend this approach to the metallic ferromagnet La0.7Sr0.3MnO3, obtaining crack-free membranes on Si that preserve ferromagnetism and metallicity.

title: Thermodynamic topology and orbital dynamics of charged RN--AdS black hole with logarithmic corrections
summary: This study investigates the topological thermodynamic properties and orbital dynamics of the Reissner--Nordström anti-de Sitter (RN--AdS) black hole with logarithmic corrections solution in Einstein--Maxwell gravity. By utilizing the Duan's $Φ$-mapping theory, we investigate the topological classes within the generalized three-parameter Sharma--Mittal entropy formalism. Employing different thermodynamic ensembles, including the canonical and mixed canonical ensembles, we explore the critical, divergence points and heat capacity, which help us determine the thermodynamic stability of the BH. In addition, the Hamiltonian formalism is employed to investigate the orbital and oscillatory motion of neutral test particles. By utilizing the effective potential approach, we examine the effective force, the stability of circular orbits, and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We further analyze the trajectories of test particles and derive the radial $\left(ω_{r}\right)$, latitudinal $\left(ω_θ\right)$, and azimuthal $\left(ω_φ\right)$ oscillation frequencies, together with the periastron precession frequency. This work provides key insights into the fundamental nature of Einstein--Maxwell gravity. Moreover, these results provide a comprehensive theoretical description of the orbital dynamics of the RN--AdS black hole solution and may be useful for future high-precision astrophysical observations.

title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory
comment: This paper is an expanded version of Section 5 of arXiv:2605.06465v1. Correspondingly, Section 5 of arXiv:2605.06465v2 has been shortened
summary: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos.

title: Geometric control of diffusive relaxation: spectral design, transport bounds and transverse mode isolation
summary: Geometric confinement changes both thermal relaxation and heat throughput, but these effects need not be governed by the same conduction path. We establish a distinction between serial and parallel geometries for passive, homogeneous Fourier conductors at fixed material properties, volume and length. For a reduced variable-area conductor, two logarithmic shape harmonics independently tune two selected Bloch-rate pairs, and exact local transport level sets permit spectral redistribution at fixed effective diffusivity. A nonperturbative weighted Poincaré bound, however, requires the effective axial diffusivity to vanish if the first positive insulated rate tends to zero at fixed length. This obstruction is avoided by continuous parallel paths with weak transverse exchange. Capacity-weighted networks identify the exchange mechanism, and a three-dimensional product domain provides an exact bulk realization. Its axial conductance remains $κV/L^2$, while exactly one positive insulated rate vanishes and the next approaches a positive limit set by axial, chamber and neck diffusion. The slow rate is asymptotically the transverse neck conductance times the sum of inverse chamber capacities. Spectral projection estimates translate this separation into a preparation- and readout-dependent observation window. The result is metastable retention of a temperature contrast under insulated conditions, not a second equilibrium state. It identifies when geometrical control of internal equilibration can be separated from macroscopic heat transport.

title: Altermagnetic magnon splitting in hematite: from bulk g-wave to planar i-wave
summary: Hematite is an insulating iron oxide with both a collinear antiferromagnetic and a weakly ferromagnetic phase with intriguing properties, such as long-range spin transport distances, that make it promising for spintronics applications. It has also been identified as a candidate for g-wave altermagnetism. Here, we present the results of fully relativistic ab initio calculations of the magnon properties of hematite, with a focus on altermagnetic effects. We quantitatively evaluate both the anisotropic and altermagnetic magnon band splitting as well as the magnon lifetimes. We show that dipolar interactions lead to a sizeable non-altermagnetic splitting and a hybridisation between opposite-chirality magnons resulting in a strong reduction of the spin expectation value of magnons close to the Γ point and around nodal planes, even in the collinear out-of-plane phase. Both the frequencies and the lifetimes have a large altermagnetic splitting in the $k_z = 0$ plane, which is characteristic of hematite and not generally expected for g-wave altermagnets. We compare our results to the prototypical, hexagonal g-wave altermagnet manganese telluride, which has four symmetry-protected nodal planes, whereas the fourth nodal surface in hematite is not completely fixed by symmetry. We derive implicit analytical expressions for this surface and discuss how it arises from a combination of rotational and translational symmetry, which leads to a transition to i-wave symmetry at the Brillouin zone boundary. The example of hematite reveals the trigonal altermagnets as a special case where the splitting function exhibits both bulk (g-wave) and planar (i-wave) components, and shows that the point symmetries alone are not sufficient to capture the full symmetry-determined behaviour of the splitting function.

title: Phase transitions in self-gravitating objects and black holes: Common properties and interpretations
comment: 14 pages, 7 figures. Presented at the 28th RAGtime Workshop, Opava, Czech Republic, November 2026
summary: We develop a simple analytic two-component model that links the thermal evolution of self-gravitating systems to black-hole thermodynamics. The model consists of a monatomic nonrelativistic ideal gas and an effective barotropic support calibrated by the specific heat $\hat c_V^{\rm J}(Θ)$ of a Jüttner gas. From the partition function we obtain an exact modified Bessel expression for $\hat c_V^{\rm J}(Θ)$ and supply compact Padé approximants with good accuracy across all temperatures. These inputs yield a closed virial-capacity formula, which we use to determine where the heat capacity changes sign as the support pressure becomes competitive with the thermal pressure. We then contrast this behavior with Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black holes. Despite the disparate microphysics, both systems exhibit a switch in heat-capacity behavior governed by competing pressure contributions. The surrogate model provides compact analytic insight into stability thresholds in self-gravitating systems and their black-hole analogues.

title: A full-color four-point form factor
summary: We determine the symbol and complete functions of the full-color two-loop four-point maximally helicity violating stress-tensor form factor in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, including $N^1$ double traces and $N^0$ single traces. Numerical unitarity and a master-integral bootstrap fix the result. A direct form-factor bootstrap reproduces the symbol. Permuting external legs in the planar 88-letter alphabet yields all 79 letters, while the $N^0$ terms contain four new nonclassical contributions. We also obtain the complete $N^0$ two-loop triple-collinear hard splitting functions.

title: The 1d Stochastic Dirac Operator
summary: We introduce a random Dirac operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R}^2)$ that we call $1d$ Stochastic Dirac Operator and which is indexed by two parameters $κ_0,κ$. In two companion articles, we show that this operator arises generically as the small disorder limit of one-dimensional random Schrödinger operators, thus revealing a universal behavior. In the present paper, we provide a detailed construction of this singular operator, and investigate its spectral properties. In particular, we show that its spectrum is either absolutely continuous when $κ= 0$, or pure point when $κ>0$. In the latter case, we show that the shape of the eigenfunctions is given by the exponential of a two sided Brownian motion with drift, in connection with a result of Rifkind and Virág. Finally, we establish a delicate convergence result of the sequence of eigenvalues / eigenfunctions from the finite-volume operator to the infinite-volume one.

title: Canted antiferromagnetism and spin-flop transition in honeycomb $α$-Na$_2$PrO$_3$ revealed by angle-dependent torque magnetometry up to 35 T
summary: We report angle-dependent piezocantilever torque measurements on single crystals of the honeycomb magnet $α$-Na$_2$PrO$_3$, proposed to display unconventional magnetism stabilized by anisotropic exchange interactions between spin-orbit entangled, pseudospin 1/2 Pr$^{4+}$ magnetic moments. Previous powder susceptibility observed signatures of a transition at low temperatures to antiferromagnetic order with a weak ferromagnetic moment. From the torque angular dependence in three orthogonal crystallographic planes, we infer a zero-field canted antiferromagnetic structure, with moments almost normal to the honeycomb layers, but weakly canted such as to give rise to a spontaneous magnetization along the in-plane monoclinic $a$-axis, with two magnetic domains related by time reversal. Sharp jumps in the torque angular dependence when the field projection along $a$ changes sign are interpreted as field-induced switching between the two degenerate domains with oppositely aligned ferromagnetic moments. We propose a minimal spin Hamiltonian including easy-axis exchange anisotropy and symmetry-allowed Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) couplings, for which mean-field calculations reproduce the main features of the observed angle-dependent torque. Torque measurements up to 35 T applied almost normal to the layers observe a strong anomaly attributed to proximity to the field-induced spin-flop transition predicted for the above Hamiltonian. We contrast the predicted magnetic phase diagrams for magnetic fields in different orthogonal crystallographic planes normal to the honeycomb layers and discuss how DM interactions convert some transitions into smooth crossovers and stabilize a phase boundary line connecting the spin-flop transition in field normal to the layers to magnetization saturation for in-plane field normal to $a$; such a phase boundary line does not exist in the absence of DM interactions.

title: Revisiting Kerr-Newman-(A)dS Black Holes in \(f(R)\) Gravity: A Kerr-Schild Approach
comment: 13 pages, no figures. Preprint of an article submitted for consideration in International Journal of Geometric Methods in Modern Physics \c{opyright} 2026 World Scientific Publishing Company, https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscinet/ijgmmp
summary: It is known that, in the constant-curvature regime, the field equations of $f(R)$ gravity reduce to the Einstein form with an effective cosmological constant, establishing a direct correspondence between stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions in $f(R)$ gravity and their counterparts in general relativity, including the Kerr--Newman--(A)dS family. Within this framework, we revisit the derivation of these metrics using the Kerr--Schild approach for illustrative purposes. The Maxwell equations are solved independently of the Kerr--Schild function, allowing the electromagnetic source to be determined before addressing the gravitational field equations. We then investigate the possibility of non-constant-curvature solutions, taking quadratic $f(R)$ gravity as a representative model. Remarkably, the field equations within the Kerr--Schild ansatz force the Ricci scalar to be constant, reducing the resulting geometries to the familiar Kerr--Newman--(A)dS family. Thus, our analysis extends the recently established no-go result for uncharged black holes to electrically charged configurations within the framework considered here.

title: Two Faces of Spacetime Density Matrices: Entanglement and Complexity
summary: We establish a direct connection between entanglement and complexity through spacetime density matrices. For stationary pure states and complementary regions at different times, spacetime replica moments encode the return amplitude of a replica-defect quench. This representation defines an associated state spread complexity, which we call Krylov-Rényi complexity. It can equivalently be obtained by using a replica-defect excitation of the replicated background state as the seed and evolving it under the original replicated Hamiltonian. We further construct Krylov-von Neumann complexity as a probe limit from first-order replica data. Timelike entanglement and complexity provide complementary information at a fixed time, while the full time dependence of the timelike entropy determines the Krylov dynamics and hence the complexity. The replica construction fixes the seed and its evolution through the background state, subsystem geometry, and regulator, without an independently chosen probe operator. Like entanglement entropy, the resulting complexity is defined nonperturbatively and probes universal properties and dynamical information about the underlying theory.

title: Moduli of continuity preserved by the Hilbert Transform
summary: It has long been known that the Hilbert transform preserves certain moduli of continuity such as Hölder continuity. In~\cite{GS01}, M. Goldstein and W. Schlag provided a criterion, based on two simple conditions, for a modulus of continuity to be preserved under the Hilbert transform. These conditions are not satisfied by the weak-Hölder and the log-Hölder moduli of continuity. More recently, A. Avila, Y. Last, M. Shamis and Q. Zhou proved in~\cite{ALSZ21} that for compactly supported $t$-log-Hölder continuous functions ($t>1$) their Hilbert transforms are at least $(t-1)$-log-Hölder continuous. A similar result holds for weak-Hölder continuous functions. In this note we extend these results to a class of continuous functions satisfying a couple of mild integrability conditions.

title: Learning Spin Hamiltonians from Interacting Magnon Spectra
summary: A neural network that learns an inverse map inherits the approximations of the forward solver used to generate its training data. We demonstrate this in the inference of spin Hamiltonians from synthetic neutron-scattering spectra and show how a fast many-body solver can overcome the limitation of linear spin-wave theory (LSWT). We consider a family of anisotropic triangular-lattice spin Hamiltonians at fields just above saturation, where magnon interactions shift and broaden the spectrum in ways that LSWT cannot capture. Using the truncated Hilbert-space ladder (THL) method, we compute the dynamical spin structure factor (DSSF) nonperturbatively within the one- and two-magnon space. THL is fast enough to generate large training sets of DSSF spectra, enabling us to train neural networks that accurately predict Hamiltonian parameters. By empirically benchmarking several neural-network architectures, we find that a one-dimensional convolutional network performs best. A learned forward decoder then reconstructs the DSSF from the predicted parameters, providing a rapid self-consistency check and a visualization of the predicted response. When interactions are strong, networks trained on LSWT and THL spectra infer markedly different parameters. Analysis of the Fisher information matrix shows that the measurement protocol, including which spin-correlation components are resolved and the momentum cut, determines which couplings can be identified. Combining machine learning with fast many- body theory is therefore essential for quantitative Hamiltonian inference from scattering data.

title: Log-periodic radiation cores and light rings in pure quadratic bulk gravity
summary: In the pure quadratic model of the Böhmer--Jensko bulk--boundary formulation of gravity, every static metric with a regular centre has vanishing central density and pressure, so no affine equation of state admits a regular non-vacuum star. We therefore study singular cores, in scale-invariant variables in which the isotropy condition is a single autonomous relation between two functions. Closures that keep the self-similar solutions as equilibria fix the stability of two vacuum lines but leave that of the matter-bearing equilibria undetermined, except at one unphysical point, so only an equation of state yields definite dynamics. For a linear equation of state the closed system has a focus, a saddle, and a vacuum point with nonzero bulk scalar that exchanges stability with the saddle in a transcritical bifurcation. At the radiation value the system is integrable, through the Tolman integral and scale invariance, and the focus becomes a nonlinear centre surrounded by log-periodic solutions. Radiation is also exactly where the line containing the matter-bearing equilibria of this closure coincides with the line of circular null orbits. Consequently every periodic radiation core with monotonic areal radius has exactly one stable and one unstable light ring per period, at radii forming two interlaced geometric progressions towards the centre with a common ratio tending to 2.165 for small oscillations. In the optical geometry the self-similar solution is a cylinder and each core a periodic tube, whose bulges and necks carry these rings. MIT bag-model configurations whose cores approach these orbits inherit this structure.

title: Second-order formulation of chiral fermions with a local boundary condition
summary: Chiral fermions in $d$ dimensions arise naturally as boundary modes of a massive fermion in $d+1$ dimensions subject to a local boundary condition. When anomalies are absent, this construction can be used to define an intrinsically $d$-dimensional theory of chiral fermions. However, defining the path integral using the first-order Dirac operator with this boundary condition is technically inconvenient, even in the continuum. We present a formulation in terms of second-order differential operators that is completely equivalent to the original formulation in the continuum. Its natural lattice discretization generates Wilson's term and avoids fermion doubling. Our lattice formulation closely resembles the boundary-fermion construction of Shamir, and provides some insight into the case of a general Wilson parameter.

title: Variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups
summary: We develop fixed-step variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups, derive their reduced dynamics, and analyze their long-time behavior by backward error analysis. We derive the continuous Euler-Lagrange equations, energy balance, and Noether conservation laws, and construct time-indexed discrete Lagrangians using retractions, with the midpoint-Cayley scheme treated explicitly. On their regularity domains, the resulting phase-space maps are symplectic. For left-invariant discrete Lagrangians, they reduce to Lie-Poisson maps that preserve coadjoint orbits and, when $G$ is connected, every Casimir function. A variational error analysis establishes second-order accuracy of the midpoint-Cayley method. We also construct an exactly symplectic, projectable extension on $T^*(\mathbb R\times G)$ whose formal modified Hamiltonian is affine in the momentum conjugate to time and admits symmetry reduction. Under uniform analyticity, coefficient bounds, and domain-containment assumptions, optimal truncation yields exponentially accurate interpolation and near-conservation of the modified extended Hamiltonian over exponentially long intervals. For a connected attitude network on $SO(3)^N$ with damping and uniformly positive, non-increasing coupling weights, we prove local asymptotic stability of the static consensus set for the continuous dynamics and exact preservation of total spatial momentum by the discrete scheme. Numerical experiments on the network and on a time-dependent rigid body on $SO(3)$ illustrate second-order convergence and the extended energy balance.

title: Symmetry-resolved spectroscopy of truncation-induced perturbations in loop tensor network renormalization of the six-vertex model
summary: Tensor network renormalization at finite bond dimension $χ$ introduces truncation errors that are amplified by the renormalization-group (RG) flow. For loop tensor network renormalization (LoopTNR) on the $c=1$ critical line of the six-vertex model, with Luttinger parameter $K$, we identify these errors operator by operator from symmetry-resolved transfer-matrix spectra and conformal perturbation theory. With $O(2)$ symmetry imposed, the dominant error is the dimerization operator, which is allowed because LoopTNR breaks one-site translation. With less symmetry it is the $U(1)$ current or a charge-two vertex operator. The growth of the dimerization per RG step and a parameter-free ratio of its amplitudes agree with conformal perturbation theory to within a few percent. The parameter $K$ drifts slowly, owing to a weak marginal error and to the running induced by the dimerization. A larger $χ$ lowers the initial amplitude of the error for $0.75\le K\le 1.5$ but changes neither the operator nor its growth rate.

title: Notes on non-equilibrium thermodynamics of Robinson-Trautman spacetimes
summary: Robinson-Trautman spacetimes are determined by a parabolic heat-type evolution equation of fourth order for a scalar field on future null infinity. This equation may be re-written as an energy balance for an asymptotically time-like observer. In turn, it becomes a first law in the context of non-equilibrium thermodynamics if the non-linear memory is interpreted as heat. This leads to a local version of temperature and a manifestly increasing entropy density from the viewpoint of the environment.

title: Holographic Tessellations Tensor Networks $\{p,q\}$ from Entangled Quantum Tetrahedron in Loop Quantum Gravity
summary: The relationship between spin network states in loop quantum gravity and bulk--boundary duality is further explored using the tessellated holographic tensor network. We develop a holographic tensor network construction based on quantum entanglement between tetrahedra in loop quantum gravity (LQG). This construction relates four-valent intertwiner spaces and Bell states dressed with $SU(2)$ holonomies to effective tensors on hyperbolic $\{p,q\}$ tessellations. For the $\{5,4\}$ tessellation, six tetrahedra are assembled into a single effective cell with five network legs and one logical index. Provided that the microscopic transfer map has full row rank, a right inverse and a completion on the kernel space are employed to construct an isometric embedding, yielding an effective tensor proportional to a perfect tensor. The construction is generalized to the $p=2n-1$ family, with local dimensions supporting absolutely maximally entangled states. On finite networks satisfying a radial orientation condition, an appropriate normalization produces an isometric bulk--boundary map. For cuts satisfying the isometry condition on both sides, the boundary entropy decomposes into a link contribution $\sum_{\ell}\log(2j_{\ell}+1)$ and the bulk entropy, thereby providing a discrete realization of the quantum Ryu--Takayanagi structure. Applications to the black hole interior are formulated via postselection-based non-isometric encoding. Assuming additional Haar statistics, this framework is used to analyze the preservation of overlaps on average and the competition between entropy branches underlying the Page Curve. These results establish a constructive link between the geometric degrees of freedom of LQG and holographic codes, while clarifying the conditions required to connect them to geometric area in LQG, the location of the quantum extremal surface, and evaporation of black hole.

title: Dynamical edge universality and the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
summary:
We prove dynamical edge universality for three families of interacting particle systems for every $β>0$: $β$-Dyson Brownian motion with an analytic potential, weighted $β$-corners processes, and a class of discrete-time Markov chains. Our results apply to general non-equilibrium initial data and show that the Airy$_β$ line ensemble emerges at positive times whenever the limiting density has a regular square-root edge.
  More precisely, after centering at the moving deterministic edge and rescaling space and time on the $n^{-2/3}$ and $n^{-1/3}$ scales, respectively, the trajectories of the top $k$ particles converge jointly in distribution to the top $k$ curves of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble, for every fixed $k$, in the topology of uniform convergence on compact time intervals.
  The proof combines dynamical loop equations with characteristic-flow estimates to establish local laws near the moving edge and upper bounds on the extremal particle. We then identify the stochastic evolution of every subsequential limit of the rescaled Stieltjes transform and establish convergence through the pole-evolution characterization of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble.

title: Circuit model for gate-induced excitation of quantum Hall edges tuned by DC gate bias
summary: Edge excitations, which propagate along the edge of a quantum Hall system, are of great interest in the study of low-dimensional electron systems and mesoscopic transport phenomena. In this study, we investigate the relationship between the input voltage and the excitation waveform for gate-induced excitations. By varying the offset voltage applied to the gate, we observe that the excitation waveform changes from a first-derivative-like response to a response proportional to the input waveform in the time domain. In the frequency domain, we observe that the frequency dependence of the gate excitation changes significantly as the offset voltage crosses the pinch-off voltage. We show that these changes can be described by a single equivalent circuit model with different effective gate-2DEG capacitances on either side of the pinch-off voltage. In addition, we confirm that the effective capacitance obtained from the fitting of the model with the experimental data is consistent with the capacitance calculated from the device structure.

title: Hyperbolic Chiral Numerical Schemes for General Relativity
summary: We develop numerical relativity evolution schemes based on Plebanski's chiral formulation of general relativity and its 3+1 form, Ashtekar's variables. At the linear level, we construct a two-parameter family of first-order gauge fixings that dynamically fixes both diffeomorphisms and internal SO(3,C) rotations; after a linear field redefinition, the resulting system splits into independent 12- and 4-component sectors. Lifting this gauge fixing to its minimal nonlinear extension and performing the 3+1 decomposition yields a strongly hyperbolic modification of Ashtekar's evolution equations that remains polynomial in the fields and includes constraint damping. We also introduce a conformal (unimodular) reformulation in which the nonlinear 12-component sector evolves completely independently of the remaining fields. All three systems are tested with gauge-wave convergence tests, robust-stability tests on a noisy Minkowski background, and long-time evolutions. The unmodified Ashtekar system crashes at T ~ 325, whereas the gauge-fixed hyperbolic and conformal systems remain stable up to T = 2000, with constraint violations and the imaginary part of the metric remaining at the 10^{-10} level.

title: Worldsheet Effective Theory of Abelian-Higgs Cosmic Strings beyond Nambu--Goto
comment: 26 pages (13 for main text, 13 for appendices). 8 figures (6 in main text). Movies of the simulations can be found in https://youtu.be/tlT1DMFg6DY and https://youtu.be/O7oJLk80Ce4 . Comments are welcome
summary: Cosmic strings can support long-lived excitations confined to their cores, opening channels for energy exchange with the transverse Goldstone modes that describe the string's motion. We derive a covariant worldsheet theory of their coupled dynamics directly from the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling, with all interaction coefficients fixed by the microscopic theory. The resulting action, which we validate against numerical lattice field theory simulations, extends the Nambu--Goto description to include a massive scalar shape mode and a massive vector mode. Dualizing the vector reveals a geometric distinction: the shape scalar mode couples to intrinsic worldsheet curvature, while the pseudoscalar couples to normal bundle curvature. These interactions explain the distinct parametric instabilities observed in lattice simulations and predict how the relative polarization of colliding transverse waves controls the excitation of the two internal modes. Our results connect microscopic string structure to the nonlinear worldsheet dynamics, providing a predictive framework for cosmic strings beyond the Nambu--Goto approximation.

title: Periods, isomonodromy, and modularity of ALG/ALG$^*$ gravitational instantons
summary: We prove that every smooth ALG or ALG$^*$ gravitational instanton of type $A_0,A_1,A_2,D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3$ is, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, isometric to a rank-two wild Hitchin moduli space on $\PP^1$ with its $L^2$ metric. We compute the compact hyperkähler periods and asymptotic parameters of these moduli spaces and give explicit inverse formulas for every admissible choice of these data. For the three ALG types, global isomonodromic transport realizes the two real parameters left undetermined by the compact periods. We use a Hamiltonian variation formula and uniform comparison with the semiflat metric to apply the Torelli and uniqueness theorems.

title: Magnetic order in Tb and Dy substituted La3Ni2O7 and effects of high-pressure high-temperature O2 annealing
summary: To study the influence of magnetic lanthanide (Ln) substituents on La3Ni2O7, polycrystalline samples of La3-xLnxNi2O7 (Ln = Pr, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, and Yb) were synthesized and characterized by electrical transport, magnetization, and x-ray and neutron powder diffraction before and after high-pressure high-temperature oxygen annealing. The annealing process led to the formation of La3Ni2O7 polymorphs and more metallic-like temperature dependence of the electrical resistance while changing the density-wave transition temperature only slightly. For unannealed La2.7Tb0.3Ni2O7 and La2.7Dy0.3Ni2O7, distinct features in the magnetic susceptibility and additional magnetic peaks in neutron diffraction patterns indicate that both samples develop long-range magnetic order below ~13 and 11 K, respectively. The magnetic signatures were strongly suppressed following oxygen annealing, suggesting a possible association with the accompanying structural modifications. These behaviors distinguish Tb and Dy from Pr, Nd, and Sm substituents which do not introduce magnetic ordering in the system, establishing La3-xTbxNi2O7 and La3-xDyxNi2O7 as promising platforms for exploring the interplay between magnetic order and pressure-induced superconductivity in La3Ni2O7.

title: Twinor Theory in the Newton--Hooke Limit: A Nonrelativistic Schrödinger Equation for Arbitrary Spin
summary: The Newton--Hooke limit of the massive twinor field equations is derived at fixed particle mass and fixed cosmological acceleration per unit displacement. On a static torsion-free background, removal of the rest energy separates the leading spin amplitude from a finite sequence of auxiliary spinors. For every positive integer rank $2s$, a regular limit of exact solutions satisfies a first-order hierarchy. Its lowest two equations give a necessary Schrödinger equation for the leading amplitude, with a curvature term from the ordered spatial derivatives and a source determined by two projections of the relativistic source. The higher equations impose additional conditions. On the homogeneous Newton--Hooke background with trivial internal connection and nonzero cosmological acceleration parameter, vanishing of all limiting contracted sources forces the leading amplitude to vanish for $s\geq\tfrac32$. A separate reduction of the scalar wave equation gives the spin-zero case.

title: Equilibrium relativistic spin magnetohydrodynamics from chiral kinetic theory
summary: We develop a microscopic and thermodynamically consistent framework for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics of massless chiral fermions, directly from first-order chiral kinetic theory. Starting from the covariant Wigner function, we recast the chiral kinetic equation as a pure streaming equation on a magnetically shifted mass shell, incorporating both the magnetic-moment energy and the Berry-curvature phase-space measure. This formulation yields a kinetic $H$-theorem and an entropy current with vanishing divergence in global equilibrium. We construct the equilibrium distribution for an arbitrary spin frame and derive the associated currents, energy--momentum tensor, spin tensor, entropy current, and frame-independent spin polarization, including the magnetic splitting between particles and antiparticles. Thermodynamic consistency further determines the second-order magnetovortical responses, revealing a relativistic Barnett magnetization, a temperature- and chemical-potential-independent anomalous charge density, and rotation-induced density corrections that reproduce exact field-theory results. Our framework provides a unified microscopic foundation for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics and establishes a direct link between quantum kinetic theory, spin polarization, magnetization, and anomalous transport.

title: Invariants of subfactors associated to Petrescu's Hadamard matrices of order 7
summary:
Petrescu's sixth-root $7 \times 7$ Hadamard matrix defines an irreducible, hyperfinite subfactor $N \subset M$ with Jones index 7. It is built from the spin model commuting square obtained from the Hadamard matrix by iterating Jones' basic construction. We prove that the standard invariant of this subfactor is minimal, i.e. the higher relative commutants consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Thus, the principal graphs of the subfactor are the Coxeter-Dynkin graph A$_\infty$. This solves a long-standing open problem. The main new idea is a congruence for the profile of the Hadamard matrix that restricts the order of rotation on the lowest-weight spaces in Jones planar algebra description of the standard invariant. Together with a uniform trace bound, this gives bounded annular multiplicities on a subsequence, which forces the principal graph to have norm at most two. We also show that the same result holds for most Hadamard matrices in Petrescu's one-parameter family. Specifically, the associated subfactors have Temperley-Lieb standard invariant at every transcendental phase and at every algebraic phase with residue $\pm1$ at a prime above three. In each fixed degree the exceptional set is finite and consists of algebraic numbers.
  Our methods apply to several other families of Hadamard matrices of order $q >4$ as well, and we show that the associated subfactors have A$_\infty$ principal graphs. These include real Hadamard matrices of order $q\equiv4\pmod8$, Hadamard matrices over $\Q(i)$ of order $q\equiv2\pmod4$ and cube-root matrices of order $q$ with $3\mid q$ and $9\nmid q$. For order six Hadamard matrices, we obtain the same result at every transcendental phase in Diţă's family through Haagerup's matrix and at every algebraically independent pair of phases in Karlsson's two-parameter family.

title: Weakly coordinating anions and solvents break the conductivity-transference-solvation tradeoff
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to Science. Under review
summary: Lithium-metal batteries promise high energy density, but common electrolytes trade ionic conductivity against the share of current carried by lithium ions and against how strongly solvent binds those ions. We show that simultaneously weakening both interactions of the lithium ion, with solvent and with anion, relaxes this trade-off. Thus, a weakly coordinating perfluorinated alkoxyaluminate salt in liquefied fluoromethane conducts 39.2 mS cm$^{-1}$ at 25 $^\circ$C while maintaining a lithium-ion transference number of 0.71. Molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that the anion prevents persistent ion aggregation and lowers the salt's dissociation penalty. Consistent with these properties, nickel-rich cathode/lithium-metal anode full cells charge at 10C at room temperature and at 2C at $-40$ $^\circ$C. We advance coordination strength as a design axis for future energy storage devices.

title: Low-Latency Alerts of Massive Black Hole Binaries in LISA
summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) for days to months before merger, offering opportunities for advance electromagnetic follow-up. To enable such observations, inference methods must provide rapid, continuously updated, and statistically calibrated posterior estimates, while remaining robust to overlapping sources. We present TRUFFLE (Time-evolving Rapid Updates For Follow-up of LISA Events), a simulation-based inference method for MBHBs in LISA data designed to meet these requirements. Our approach uses two networks, selected according to the time to coalescence relative to the end of the analysis window, $Δt_c$. An early-warning network, operating at $Δt_c \in [4~\mathrm{h}, 2~\mathrm{d}]$, estimates the chirp mass, mass ratio, and coalescence time to support electromagnetic follow-up scheduling. A near-merger network, operating at $Δt_c \in [-1~\mathrm{h}, +4~\mathrm{h}]$, infers nine parameters, including the sky position needed for telescope pointing. Both networks process the most recent six days of data using multiband time- and frequency-domain representations, which are summarized by a transformer to condition a normalizing flow. The networks are trained on the full orbit-driven LISA response and amortized over a 30-day range of observation epochs. The near-merger posterior can be corrected through likelihood-based importance sampling, with neural inference taking seconds and likelihood reweighting approximately five minutes on a single GPU. We obtain unbiased posteriors in the presence of overlapping sources, including plunging extreme-mass-ratio inspirals, resolvable Galactic binaries, and additional MBHBs merging up to two hours before the primary merger.

title: Cardinal RG=GR: Phase-Space Cardinality and the Cosmological Constant and Hierarchy Problems
summary: The effective field theory approach constructs the low-energy theory by integrating out fluctuations above an ultraviolet scale which raises the cosmological constant and hierarchy problems. We investigate an alternative prescription in which the quantum theory is restricted to a finite accessible region of phase space, characterized by a dimensionless cardinality $\mathcal N$, rather than by independently prescribed spacetime and momentum scales. At fixed cardinality these scales are related. For Euclidean de Sitter space, the stationarity condition for the gravitational action can then be written as a stationarity condition with respect to the momentum scale, a relation which we call Cardinal RG=GR. We demonstrate the relation between $\mathcal N$ and the Gibbons-Hawking entropy of de Sitter space, compute the cosmological constant proportional to ${1}/{\sqrt{\mathcal N}}$, show that it is radiatively stable and apply the same prescription to demonstrate the radiative stability of the mass parameter for a simple interacting scalar field model, thereby illuminating the resolution of the hierarchy problem. We also establish a precise limit, involving gravitational data, in which the conventional results of Quantum Field Theory and the Renormalization Group are recovered.

title: Asymptotics of Hitchin metrics and modularity of exceptional ALG gravitational instantons
summary: We prove asymptotic estimates for the Hitchin metrics on four-dimensional moduli spaces of parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(n,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere with flag types corresponding to the Dynkin types $E_6$, $E_7$ and $E_8$. For fixed weights in the alcove interiors and fixed scalar graded residues, the Hitchin metric converges in $C^\infty$ to the semiflat metric along the end. The decay is polynomial in general and exponential when all graded residues vanish. For every admissible parameter with weights in the closed alcoves, the moduli space with its Hitchin metric is a complete nonflat ALG gravitational instanton of order two. Extending the period calculation of Dimakis--Fredrickson--Yae to the boundary and allowing compactly supported changes of marking, we obtain every point of the normalized period domain. It follows from the ALG Torelli theorem that every ALG gravitational instanton with cone parameter $1/3$, $1/4$ or $1/6$ is isometric, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, to one of these moduli spaces with its Hitchin metric.

title: Generalized Critical-State Analysis of Local Field Screening in High-Pressure Yttrium Polyhydride
summary: We resolve the long-standing controversy over the interpretation of magnetic-flux expulsion in high-pressure superhydrides by measuring the local magnetic field adjacent to yttrium polyhydride at 171 GPa and 4.1 K with a $^{57}$Fe Mössbauer sensor. Nuclear forward scattering tracks the local induction $B_{\rm sensor}(B_a)$, which nearly merges with the normal-state line near 1.5 T. Rather than assuming a constant-current Bean state, we solve the critical-state problem for the actual thin-disk geometry using the Shantsev--Clem--Sanchez method and compare generalized field-dependent critical-state models. Both the Kim and exponential laws reproduce the measured virgin branch, whereas the constant-$J_c$ Bean model fails. The corresponding zero-field critical-current densities, $(4.38\pm1.48)\times10^{11}$ and $(2.45\pm0.22)\times10^{11}$ A/m$^2$, respectively, are consistent in order of magnitude with transport estimates for granular YH$_6$. These results establish that the observed flux expulsion is a pinned critical state, not the equilibrium Meissner effect, and demonstrate a general methodology for probing local superconductivity under extreme conditions.

title: Bianchi cosmologies with four-dimensional groups of motion in New General Relativity
summary: We study the dynamics of the most general metric teleparallel spacetimes of Bianchi types II, III and IX, which admit a four-dimensional symmetry group, in the 1-parameter family of New General Relativity. We first show that in each of these classes the most general metric teleparallel geometry is described by four free functions of time, while another four functions of time describe the most general energy-momentum tensor compatible with the same symmetries. We then derive the field equations of New General Relativity for this class of geometries. Finally, we present some solutions to these field equations. Our results show that both solutions resembling features of the standard Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker cosmology of General Relativity and deviations thereof exist.

title: Full-Color Two-loop Four-point Form Factor in N=4 SYM with Global CK-duality
summary: We determine the full-color two-loop four-point MHV form factor of the stress-tensor supermultiplet in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory. Using color-kinematics (CK) duality and unitarity cuts, we construct complete one- and two-loop integrands manifesting global off-shell CK duality without explicit $μ^2$ dependence. Integration-by-parts reduction to uniform-transcendentality master integrals yields purely rational numbers multiplying simple kinematic prefactors, manifesting maximal transcendentality. Expressing the form factor in terms of pentagon functions, we verify full-color infrared-pole cancellation, extract the finite remainder, and obtain new non-planar results for the two-loop triple-collinear splitting function and double-soft current.

title: Propagation of chaos with singular potentials: A weighted duality approach
summary: We establish the propagation of chaos and derive the Vlasov equation from a many-body $N$-particle system in the mean-field regime with singular interaction forces bounded by $|x|^{-α-1}$ for $0\le α<(d-1)/2$ in dimensions $d\ge 2$, which in particular include the full range of sub-Coulomb interactions in three dimensions as well as the Coulomb interaction in two dimensions. Our proof is based on an energy-based framework for deriving weighted uniform bounds on cumulants that builds upon the recent duality method developed by Bresch--Duerinckx--Jabin in combination with a new Morawetz-type estimate, allowing us to remove the restriction to locally square-integrable interaction force kernels and handle more singular regimes.

title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
comment: The manuscript is 30 pages in total, including the Supporting Information. The main text is 20 pages with 4 figures and 2 tables, and the Supporting Information is 10 pages with 6 figures and 6 tables
summary: Metal halide perovskites have spin-orbit coupling among the strongest in semiconductors, yet whether their centrosymmetric bulk phases can convert charge current into spin current, and what controls the response, is unknown. Here we identify, from first-principles calculations on the four all-inorganic compounds CsBX3 (B = Pb, Sn; X = Br, I), the factors that govern their intrinsic spin Hall conductivity. The conductivity arises from the spin Berry curvature of the spin-orbit-split halide-p bands, 1.1-2.6 eV below the valence band maximum, and exceeds that of III-V and group-IV semiconductors when the Fermi level lies inside them. Because the valence band maximum is an s-p singlet, shifted only in second order, these contributions cancel in the undoped compounds, which respond like conventional semiconductors.
